words.definition: work done during a course that counts towards the final mark
words.example: My {coursework} consists of projects completed during the year, not in timed exams.

words.definition: a qualification earned by completing a university course
words.example: She studied for a bachelor's {degree} in engineering at university.

words.definition: money awarded to help someone pay for their studies
words.example: Her music {scholarship} pays half the fees at her new school.

words.definition: being present at a place you are expected to go
words.example: Perfect {attendance} means being at school every day, without missing a single session.

words.definition: one of the periods into which a school year is divided
words.example: Our school year is divided into three parts; the autumn {term} comes first.

words.definition: a teacher who gives extra help to one learner or a small group
words.example: My maths {tutor} gives me extra lessons alone after school.

words.definition: a talk given to teach a group about a subject
words.example: The professor gave a {lecture}, speaking for an hour while students listened silently.

words.definition: a practical class where people learn by doing activities together
words.example: At the pottery {workshop}, we all made clay bowls with the instructor.

words.definition: an official document showing that you have done or passed something
words.example: I received a swimming {certificate} with my name and the distance I completed.

words.definition: a visit where students stay with families in another country
words.example: On our school {exchange}, we stay with French families who later visit us.

words.definition: a statement about what you think will happen in the future
words.example: My {prediction} is that the taller plant will flower first next week.

words.definition: something noticed by watching carefully
words.example: I wrote an {observation} about what I saw: each touched leaf curled.

words.definition: a number found by checking size, weight or amount
words.example: The ruler's {measurement} shows that this leaf is eight centimetres long.

words.definition: facts or numbers collected for study
words.example: We entered all fifty temperature readings into a table of {data}.

words.definition: a small amount chosen to show what the whole is like
words.example: We tested a water {sample} taken from just one part of the lake.

words.definition: a particular way of doing something
words.example: Our {method} involves weighing each pot before and after adding water.

words.definition: something in a test that can change
words.example: The only {variable} we change is temperature; everything else stays fixed throughout the test.

words.definition: a number found by adding amounts and dividing by how many there are
words.example: The {average} of two, four and six is four.

words.definition: correct and free from mistakes
words.example: Our estimate was {accurate}: the exact count matched it, with no error.

words.definition: close to the correct amount but not exact
words.example: The {approximate} weight is ten kilograms; we have not measured it exactly.

words.definition: a set of reasons given to support an idea
words.example: The strongest {argument} in favour of later starts is that teenagers need sleep.

words.definition: the way someone sees or thinks about an issue
words.example: From a cyclist's {viewpoint}, a cycle lane matters more than extra parking.

words.definition: a plan or idea put forward for others to consider
words.example: We submitted a {proposal} for approval, with drawings of our suggested cycle lane.

words.definition: a reason given for being against a plan or idea
words.example: My {objection} to the route concerns safety: I oppose sending cyclists through that junction.

words.definition: another possibility you can choose instead
words.example: Walking is one option; taking the bus is an {alternative}.

words.definition: something that happens because of an action or situation
words.example: I arrived late as a direct {consequence} of missing the bus.

words.definition: the reason something exists or is done
words.example: The {purpose} of this button is to stop the machine in an emergency.

words.definition: a good effect that something has
words.example: We planted trees for the {benefit} of everyone who uses the park.

words.definition: an organised discussion where people argue different sides of a question
words.example: In our formal {debate}, each team had two minutes to argue its side.

words.definition: something that restricts how much can be done or known
words.example: A key {limitation} of our study is that we questioned only five people.

words.definition: to study parts of something carefully to understand it
words.example: In chemistry, we {analyse} a mixture to identify the substances it contains.

words.definition: to judge an amount roughly without measuring it exactly
words.example: We {estimate} the crowd at two hundred, because counting everyone exactly is impossible.

words.definition: to give good reasons for something you have done or believe
words.example: You must {justify} the expense by showing why spending so much was necessary.

words.definition: to reach a final judgement after thinking about information
words.example: From these results, we can {conclude} that sunlight helped the plants grow.

words.definition: to recognise or show the difference between things
words.example: Can you {distinguish} between fact and opinion, telling which is which?

words.definition: to show that one point is particularly important
words.example: The speaker will {emphasise} the key point by repeating it three times.

words.definition: to question whether something is right or true
words.example: We {challenge} the claim that all birds fly by pointing to penguins.

words.definition: to make something easier to understand
words.example: Could you {clarify} this confusing sentence by explaining exactly what you mean?

words.definition: to make someone believe something is true
words.example: The footprints may {convince} you that a fox really visited our garden.

words.definition: to accept that something is true, especially something you would rather hide
words.example: I must {admit} that I broke the window, though I fear being blamed.

words.definition: used to introduce a surprising fact after what was just said
words.example: The climb exhausted us, {yet} we reached the top instead of turning back.

words.definition: used to add another reason or point
words.example: The library is free; {besides}, it lends computers as well as books.

words.definition: used to say what will happen if something is not done
words.example: Put the milk in the fridge; {otherwise}, it may go sour.

words.definition: during the time that something else is happening
words.example: Mum cooked dinner; {meanwhile}, I set the table as she worked.

words.definition: in the end, after a long time or many difficulties
words.example: After months of practice, I {eventually} managed to swim a whole kilometre.

words.definition: only if a particular condition is met
words.example: You may borrow my bike {provided that} you return it before dinner.

words.definition: used before a fact that makes another fact surprising
words.example: I finished the book {even though} I found its opening chapters dull.

words.definition: because of something that happened before
words.example: The pipe burst; {as a result}, water flooded the kitchen floor.

words.definition: used when the next thing is very different from the last
words.example: The north was rainy; {in contrast}, the south had clear blue skies.

words.definition: without being stopped by a difficulty
words.example: We completed the walk {in spite of} the wind blowing against us.

words.definition: an organised collection of information that can be searched on a computer
words.example: The library's {database} lets staff search thousands of book records by author.

words.definition: a computer document with rows and columns for working with numbers
words.example: Our budget {spreadsheet} adds the numbers in each column automatically.

words.definition: a group of computers connected so they can exchange information
words.example: All classroom computers belong to one school {network} and share a printer.

words.definition: space used to keep information on a device
words.example: Deleting old videos frees up {storage} for more files on my tablet.

words.definition: an extra copy kept in case the original is lost
words.example: I keep a {backup} on a separate drive in case my laptop breaks.

words.definition: the ability or right to enter or use something
words.example: Only staff have {access} to this folder; pupils cannot open it.

words.definition: using computer signals to store or show information
words.example: A {digital} camera stores photographs as electronic files instead of on film.

words.definition: created by a computer to seem like a real place or experience
words.example: A {virtual} reality headset makes computer-generated worlds seem all around you.

words.definition: to put a program on a computer so it can be used
words.example: We {install} the program by copying its files into the computer's system folders.

words.definition: to use a machine to make a computer copy of paper or a picture
words.example: Please {scan} this paper drawing to create an image file on the computer.

words.definition: the work of gathering and reporting news
words.example: She studies {journalism} at college to train for a career in reporting news.

words.definition: the amount or way that news services report an event
words.example: The channel's live election {coverage} reported results from every counting centre.

words.definition: one particular version or issue of a book or newspaper
words.example: Today's morning {edition} of the newspaper was printed before the evening update.

words.definition: the number of copies of a newspaper or magazine sold regularly
words.example: The newspaper's daily {circulation} is ten thousand copies sold.

words.definition: regular payments to receive a publication or service
words.example: My magazine {subscription} delivers a new issue to my home every month.

words.definition: attention from newspapers or television intended to make people interested in something
words.example: Posters and newspaper stories gave the play {publicity}, attracting people who might buy tickets.

words.definition: an unfair preference that stops someone judging things equally
words.example: The report shows {bias} by praising one team and ignoring the other's achievements.

words.definition: likely to make someone believe something that is not true
words.example: The {misleading} headline suggests the pool closed forever, though it closed only today.

words.definition: to tell people information about something that has happened
words.example: Journalists {report} on events, telling the public what has happened and where.

words.definition: to repeat exactly what someone else has said or written
words.example: If you {quote} her, copy her exact words inside quotation marks.

words.definition: an area of land where wild animals and plants are protected
words.example: This nature {reserve} protects wild birds, and visitors must stay on marked paths.

words.definition: a building with clear walls and roof where plants are grown
words.example: Tomatoes grow in our glass {greenhouse}, which traps warmth around the plants.

words.definition: the layer of gases around a planet
words.example: Earth's {atmosphere} contains the air we breathe and surrounds the whole planet.

words.definition: a gas released when fuels burn and taken in by plants
words.example: Burning coal releases {carbon dioxide}, a gas that contributes to global warming.

words.definition: coal, oil or gas formed underground from ancient living things
words.example: Coal is a {fossil fuel} formed from plants buried millions of years ago.

words.definition: using or coming from the sun
words.example: The roof's {solar} panels use sunlight to produce electricity.

words.definition: able to continue without using up supplies or harming the natural world
words.example: A {sustainable} forest provides wood while new trees replace those cut down.

words.definition: the disappearance of every living member of an animal or plant group
words.example: Protecting their habitat could save these rare frogs from {extinction}.

words.definition: to use a supply of something such as fuel or energy
words.example: Older light bulbs {consume} more electricity than newer ones producing the same light.

words.definition: to keep something in its existing state and prevent harm or decay
words.example: Museum staff {preserve} old documents by stopping the paper from decaying.

words.definition: a person who legally belongs to a particular country
words.example: She remains a British {citizen} while living permanently abroad and holding a British passport.

words.definition: a group of people chosen to make decisions for a local area
words.example: The town {council} decides how local money is spent on parks and roads.

words.definition: an organised occasion when people choose someone by voting
words.example: Our class {election} chooses a representative through a secret ballot.

words.definition: an agreed plan or set of ideas used to guide decisions
words.example: The school's homework {policy} explains its general approach to setting work.

words.definition: an official rule made by a government that people must obey
words.example: The new {law} was passed by Parliament and is enforced by the courts.

words.definition: a situation where people have the same rights and chances
words.example: Campaigners call for {equality} before the law: the same legal rights for everyone.

words.definition: a form of government in which people choose their leaders by voting
words.example: A country is a {democracy} when its people can freely elect their government.

words.definition: being made part of a group or activity
words.example: Her {inclusion} on the team list meant she could take part in every game.

words.definition: to choose officially by marking a paper or raising your hand
words.example: We each {vote} by marking one candidate's name on a secret ballot.

words.definition: to speak or act for a person or group
words.example: Our delegate will {represent} us, speaking on our behalf at the council meeting.

words.definition: the series of jobs someone does during their working life
words.example: Her teaching {career} lasted forty years, from her first job to retirement.

words.definition: a move to a higher position at work
words.example: She received a {promotion}, moving from assistant to manager with greater responsibility.

words.definition: a person or organisation that pays people to work
words.example: The factory is the town's biggest {employer}, paying wages to five hundred workers.

words.definition: someone paid to work for a person or organisation
words.example: The company calls every paid worker an {employee}, including managers and apprentices.

words.definition: a formal written request to get a job or place on a course
words.example: I sent a job {application} explaining why the shop should hire me.

words.definition: someone being considered for a job or position
words.example: The final job {candidate} will meet the manager before she makes her choice.

words.definition: a job that is available for someone to take
words.example: The shop advertises a {vacancy} because it needs a new assistant.

words.definition: a fixed amount of money paid regularly for doing a job
words.example: Unlike bonuses, her {salary} is the fixed amount her employer pays each month.

words.definition: knowledge or skill gained by doing something yourself
words.example: She has ten years of teaching {experience} from working in several schools.

words.definition: someone who learns a skilled job while working for an experienced person
words.example: After finishing her training, the electrician stopped being an {apprentice} and became fully qualified.

words.definition: a plan for how much money you can spend
words.example: Our holiday {budget} sets a limit of fifty pounds a day.

words.definition: money that a person receives, usually from work
words.example: Her monthly {income} includes wages, rent from her flat and interest from savings.

words.definition: money spent on something you need to do or have
words.example: The largest {expense} on our trip was the cost of the hotel.

words.definition: money kept instead of spent so it can be used later
words.example: My {savings} are the money I have put aside instead of spending.

words.definition: money left after a business has paid all its costs
words.example: Sales exceeded costs by eighty pounds, so our stall made a {profit}.

words.definition: the amount by which a business spends more than it earns
words.example: Costs exceeded sales by twenty pounds, so the stall made a {loss}.

words.definition: money you owe and have not yet paid back
words.example: Paying back the money I borrowed will clear my {debt}.

words.definition: how much money something is worth
words.example: The painting's {value} rose from fifty pounds to two hundred pounds.

words.definition: cheap enough for someone to be able to pay for
words.example: This ticket is {affordable} even on my small pocket-money allowance.

words.definition: to put money into something hoping it will earn more later
words.example: People {invest} money in businesses hoping their money will grow over time.

words.definition: annoyance because something stops you doing what you want
words.example: After the printer jammed five times, my {frustration} made me want to shout.

words.definition: the ability to wait or face difficulties without becoming annoyed
words.example: Teaching a puppy takes {patience}; you must stay calm through repeated mistakes.

words.definition: the ability to understand how another person feels
words.example: I felt {empathy} with the winner's joy, imagining how happy she must be.

words.definition: words saying you are sorry for something you did wrong
words.example: My written {apology} said sorry for breaking her toy and promised to replace it.

words.definition: the feeling that you can do something successfully
words.example: Each successful performance increased my {confidence} in my ability to play well.

words.definition: the strong wish to keep trying until you succeed
words.example: Her {determination} never to give up kept her going despite failure after failure.

words.definition: words or actions that give someone hope and help them keep trying
words.example: The crowd shouted {encouragement}: 'Keep going! You can do it!'

words.definition: an agreement where each side gives up something it wanted
words.example: We reached a {compromise}: each side gave up something to reach an agreement.

words.definition: feeling happy and showing it
words.example: I felt {cheerful} this morning, smiling and humming a happy tune.

words.definition: careful to avoid causing trouble or unhappiness for others
words.example: Please be {considerate} of sleeping neighbours by keeping your music low.

words.definition: a public display of art or other objects for people to visit
words.example: The gallery's {exhibition} displays fifty paintings for visitors to see this month.

words.definition: a work of art made by shaping a solid material
words.example: The marble {sculpture} is a three-dimensional horse that visitors can walk around.

words.definition: a picture of a person, especially their face
words.example: The artist painted my {portrait} on canvas, showing my face and shoulders.

words.definition: a picture showing an area of countryside
words.example: The {landscape} on this canvas shows hills and fields, with no people.

words.definition: showing shapes and colours rather than recognisable people or objects
words.example: The {abstract} painting has only circles and lines, with no recognisable objects.

words.definition: created first, rather than copied from something else
words.example: This is the {original} drawing; the other versions are photocopies of it.

words.definition: a short performance given to try to get a part in a show
words.example: She sang at an {audition} to see whether she would get the part.

words.definition: a piece of music that someone has written
words.example: The orchestra performed her newest {composition}, a piece she wrote for strings.

words.definition: the pleasant sound of different musical notes played together
words.example: The singers' different notes blend in {harmony} rather than clashing with each other.

words.definition: a repeated pattern of beats in music
words.example: We clap the {rhythm} of the song: two short beats, then one long.

words.definition: the line separating two countries or areas
words.example: We crossed the {border} from France into Spain.

words.definition: a country's official office in another country
words.example: Our country's {embassy} in Paris is its official office in France.

words.definition: an official document used to show who you are when travelling abroad
words.example: My {passport} is a travel document containing my photograph, nationality and border stamps.

words.definition: official permission to enter or stay in a country for a period
words.example: My student {visa} allows me to stay in the country for one year.

words.definition: a person who lives in a particular place
words.example: She is a {resident} of Britain, living here without being a British citizen.

words.definition: a large area that forms part of a country or the world
words.example: This mountainous {region} covers several towns and villages in the country's north.

words.definition: a famous or easily recognised building or feature of a place
words.example: The tall clock tower is a city {landmark} that visitors easily recognise.

words.definition: buildings, traditions and objects passed down from earlier generations
words.example: Our cultural {heritage} includes old castles and songs passed down through many generations.

words.definition: easy for people, including those with disabilities, to enter or use
words.example: The museum is wheelchair {accessible}, with ramps and wide doorways throughout.

words.definition: to find and follow a way through a place
words.example: We use a compass to {navigate} across the hills without getting lost.
